Alright... @samdoran and I discussed this heavily in slack with input from bcoca, shrews, shertel, and sivel (sivel wasn't there for the end).  It changed my mind about whether install should know about site-packages.  Here's the summary:

* download, init, build, and publish are not about the collections on the system at all so they don't need to care about collection_path and whether site-packages is in there.

* list and verify should both take site-packages into account (they're similar in that they're both giving information about things that are available for use inside a playbook.)

* install deals with what's usable inside of a playbook but it's a little different:
  * We **do** want site-packages to be used when figuring out if we should install something vs already installed (reading the current state of the system).  In this context, site-packages is just another directory in the collection search path.
  * There is an annoyance factor here when someone wants to upgrade a collection that's in site-packages.  However, this annoyance exists for a collection installed into any collection path... So we probably need to solve the upgrade use-case as a general problem, not specifically for site-packages.
  * We **do not** want to install to place collections into site-packages (changing the current state of the system).  We currently achieve this by placing site-packages last in the collection search path.

I ask because I think I'm stretched too thin.  My PR implements everything that we care about knowing about site-packages but it reveals that the install/upgrade case needs to be redesigned somewhat.  If we're going to address that, I'll probably need an extra hand to help work on that.
I wonder if it's OK for ansible-base 2.10 that  `ansible-galaxy collection lists` works, though install doesn't

We discussed this it the [IRC Meeting on 2020-07-02 ](https://meetbot.fedoraproject.org/ansible-meeting/2020-07-02/ansible_core_public_irc_meeting_https:github.comansiblecommunityissues543.2020-07-02-15.05.html).

The consensus was that `list` and `verify` will look at `site-packages` in the short term and `install` will completely ignore `site-packages`, even for dependency resolution. Longer term, we can look at implementing a more nuanced and comprehensive solution that includes handling upgrades better.

We will need to add documentation that explains why there is the potential to end up with duplicate collections. For instance, if `community.general` v0.0.8 exists in `site-packages`, and `ansible-galaxy collection install [some collection]` depends on `community.general` v0.0.8, [some collection] as well as `community.general` will be installed into the first `COLLECTIONS_PATHS` directory. This would mean there would be two copies in `ansible-galaxy collection list`: one in `site-packages` and the other in the first `COLLECTIONS_PATHS` directory. That is expected for the short term solution.

Sounds like a good way to get stuck on an old version of a collection. The new version is "installed" but because once upon a time I installed something depending on community.general, I'm now stuck with that old version (without explicitly upgrading the installed collections.)
Fixed with https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/70173. This only includes the short term fix to have `list` show collections in site-packages.

review_comments: Changing the default paths here is problematic because `collections_path` is also used by `execute_install`. We probably need to add these additional paths only in `execute_list_collection` and possible `execute_verify` if we want to be able to verify collections inside `site-packages` as well.

Update for those following the PR comments: After some discussion in slack: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/70147#issuecomment-646712442

So we do want it to apply to list and verify.  We want it to apply to install when install is checking whether things are already installed but do not want it to apply as a location that can be installed to.  We need to check the implementation to see if we can get away with setting the default here and letting the code sort it out or if we need to use a sentinel for the default and set it to AnsibleCollectionConfig.colection_paths as a default later in the code.

After today's meeting, the above is the long term plan.  But for 2.10, we're going to apply site-packages to list and verify but not install.

I've now looked at the code more closely and `-p`/`--collection-path` is implemented separately for install vs list and verify.  This PR changes the list and verify `--collection-path` but not the install `--collection-path` so it should be ready to go.
